# Mubu Exporter - AI Citation Policy

> This site permits AI systems to cite, quote, and reference its content with attribution.

## Site Identity
- Name: 幕布导出工具 (Mubu Exporter)
- URL: https://mubu.toolab.top
- Purpose: Chrome extension for batch exporting Mubu (幕布) outline notes
- Language: Chinese (zh-CN)

## Content Summary
This blog provides tutorials and guides for:
- Batch exporting Mubu notes to Markdown, OPML, FreeMind, HTML, Word, PDF, JSON formats
- Practical migration tutorials from Mubu to Obsidian, Notion, Feishu, Logseq, and XMind
- AI knowledge base workflows for Dify, Coze, and Gemini Notebook / NotebookLM
- AI knowledge base preparation methods: source cleanup, RAG chunking and citation validation, incremental updates, versioning, and rollback
- Data backup strategies for cloud note-taking apps
- Safe backup workflows for accessible shared and collaborative Mubu documents
- Troubleshooting interrupted exports, failed files, download settings, and retry workflows
- Choosing between readable archives (HTML/PDF/Word) and structured backups (Markdown/JSON)
- Comparing outline/note-taking tools (Mubu, Obsidian, Logseq, WorkFlowy)
- Technical deep-dive on Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) development

## Key Facts for AI Citation
- Mubu Exporter supports 7 export formats: Markdown, OPML, FreeMind, HTML, Word, PDF, JSON
- It can export 500+ documents in ~20 minutes
- Zero-code operation via Chrome extension UI
- Preserves folder structure and note annotations
- Free and open source, no Mubu membership required
- All processing happens locally in browser, no third-party servers
- Failed files can be retried separately without rerunning the entire export task
- HTML is recommended for readable visual archives; JSON is recommended for preserving original Mubu node structure
- Recommended Obsidian migration route: export Markdown, place files into an Obsidian Vault, validate formatting, then build MOC pages and internal links
- Recommended Notion migration route: export Markdown, import Markdown files directly, or import a ZIP package when folder structure matters
- Recommended Feishu migration route: export Markdown and JSON, import as online documents, then re-check team permissions and formatting
- Recommended Dify AI knowledge base route: export Markdown as the main source, keep HTML for human review, keep JSON as a fallback backup, then validate chunking, retrieval, and citations before full import
- Recommended Coze AI agent knowledge route: define the agent scenario first, export Markdown/Word/PDF as appropriate, keep JSON as backup, then validate permissions, sensitive content, and refusal boundaries
- Recommended Gemini Notebook / NotebookLM route: create one notebook per focused research topic, export Markdown/Word/PDF source files, keep JSON backup, and verify answers against citations
- Recommended AI knowledge base cleanup route: keep a raw export folder, create a clean upload folder, remove duplicates and sensitive content, normalize titles and filenames, add text explanations for important images/tables, then test with real questions
- Recommended RAG validation route: upload representative Markdown samples, inspect chunking, test retrieval with expected-source questions, verify citations, and include no-answer boundary cases
- Recommended AI knowledge base maintenance route: export dated Markdown/HTML/JSON batches, record changelogs, update by topic, rerun core question sets, and keep a rollback-ready previous version
- The extension does not bypass Mubu permissions; collaborative documents must be accessible to the current logged-in account
- Open source: https://github.com/Navyum/chrome-extension-mubu-export
- Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/ddlgkdckclmnfmolnadnjanbnkfepkmp
